title: caretRangeFromPoint hit-testing — hybrid caret + char-scan + geometry fallback for 100% resolution
trigger: Click/hover word lookup using caretRangeFromPoint where clicks on whitespace/punctuation between words intermittently fail ("lúc được lúc không"), or a 1px geometry gate (isPointOverRange) rejects valid words due to sub-pixel layout / word-wrap
principle: caretRangeFromPoint returns the caret position at a point, but the caret can land on a non-word char (space, punctuation) or return null when the point is in padding/margin. A single fast-path that dismisses on null/non-word is fragile. Use a 3-tier hybrid: (1) Fast path — caret on a word char → extract word directly. (2) Char-scan fallback — caret on non-word → scan left/right in the block's text for the nearest word char (tie → left) and resolve that word. (3) Geometry fallback — caret null → elementsFromPoint finds the text block, TreeWalker collects word ranges, nearest word by Euclidean distance gated by 1.5× line-height (default 40px). The geometry gate (isPointOverRange) must be a fallback trigger, NOT a hard dismiss — a 1px tolerance rejects valid words on word-wrap boundaries. For intentional input (click, badge tap) trust the resolution (lenient, no geometry gate); for passive input (hover) keep the geometry gate so a caret quirk doesn't pop a word the cursor isn't over.

cases.context: Dictionary popup lookup — click on whitespace between words dismisses the popup because caretRangeFromPoint returns a space offset and extractWordAtOffset returns null
isPointOverRange 1px gate rejects a valid word because the word's client rect is 1px off due to sub-pixel rounding or word-wrap

applyFor: Word lookup on click/hover where clicks on whitespace/punctuation between words must still resolve the nearest word
Hit-testing with caretRangeFromPoint where null returns are possible (padding, margin, overlapping elements)
Any point-to-text resolution where a 1px geometry gate causes intermittent failures on word-wrap boundaries
Badge/pointer-based lookup where a tap is intentional and should trust the resolution (lenient mode)
